response.rationale: High fecal calprotectin and diffuse colonic inflammation strongly support ulcerative colitis, while low CEA and negative stool tests argue against cancer and infection. The PET-avid focus is nonspecific and can reflect inflammation.

rejected.why: Low CEA (1.7) and diffuse inflammatory thickening favor UC over malignancy; PET avidity can be inflammatory.
Current CT shows diffuse colitis, not localized diverticulitis; prior possible diverticulitis is not the dominant finding.
